stories.title: How Thailand’s Limestone Islands Formed
stories.subtitle: From an ancient seabed to the dramatic towers of Phang Nga Bay
stories.description: Discover how ancient sea sediments became limestone, how rainwater carved tall rock towers, and why those towers now rise from the sea. Practise useful English with Armenian vocabulary support, reading questions, and speaking prompts.

media.alt: Ko Tapu limestone sea stack surrounded by the green waters and cliffs of Phang Nga Bay, Thailand.
media.caption: The limestone towers of Phang Nga Bay began as sediments beneath an ancient sea.
media.changes: Wikimedia thumbnail; displayed with responsive cropping.

media.alt: A steep, vegetation-covered limestone tower rises from the sea in Phang Nga Bay.
media.caption: Water gradually widened cracks and removed surrounding limestone, leaving steep towers.

stories.title: Maya Bay: Stone, Cinema, and a Second Chance
stories.subtitle: An illustrated journey through ancient limestone, a famous film, a living sea, and the work of recovery.
stories.description: Explore the complete story of Maya Bay: its ancient cliffs, turquoise water, people and film history, the 2018 closure, the latest 2026 conservation evidence, and how to visit thoughtfully. Includes five real photographs, two maps, a geology diagram, and a full English lesson with Armenian vocabulary.

media.alt: Turquoise water at Maya Bay framed by steep green limestone cliffs and coastal vegetation in March 2026.
media.caption: Maya Bay photographed on 17 March 2026. The limestone walls frame a real opening to the Andaman Sea.

media.alt: White sand and translucent shallow water in Maya Bay, with boats near the rocky opening, photographed in 2007.
media.caption: White sand and shallow water at Maya Bay, 2 March 2007. This historical photograph predates the 2018 closure and later visitor rules.

media.alt: A 2017 view from beneath a rock overhang showing many boats in Maya Bay.
media.caption: Boats in Maya Bay on 11 June 2017, before the 2018 closure. The image records an earlier pattern of tourism, not current access arrangements.

media.alt: Steep weathered limestone cliffs above the pale beach and blue-green water of Maya Bay.
media.caption: The limestone walls and pale beach of Maya Bay, photographed on 11 March 2007. The rock is far older than the present shoreline.

media.alt: Boats inside Pileh Lagoon among tall green limestone walls, photographed in 2018.
media.caption: Pileh Lagoon on Phi Phi Leh, 6 June 2018. This is a different inlet from Maya Bay; the two places are often included in the same island excursion.

media.alt: Regional map placing Maya Bay on Phi Phi Leh southeast of Phuket and south of Krabi, with separate markers for Phi Phi Don, Karon, Phuket Town, Ao Nang and Krabi Town.
media.caption: Maya Bay in its regional setting. Coastlines use Natural Earth data; place markers are approximate. This orientation map is not for navigation.
